RESEARCH COLLECTION / FLAGSHIPS 71–80 OF 90

Botanical Networks, Skin Aging & Adaptive Skincare at the Limit

STARLI Herbal Skincare  |  F71–F80 / 90  |  Author 33  |  Research Design Working Edition v1.2

This ten-volume prospective, nonclinical collection examines botanical antioxidant interaction, energy-limited nanocarrier transport, microbiome resilience, stress-memory reversibility, epigenetic age uncertainty, optical versus biological aging, bounded feedback control, personalized forecasting, responsive facial masks and safe formulation search. Each flagship is a proposed research contract, not evidence of cosmetic efficacy.

Two five-theme units contain ten English 777-page working editions: 300 conditional formula plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 separately paginated study designs, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Experimental tests, independent physical witnesses and hard-stop boundaries must be distinguished from editorial structure.

Research Unit I · F71–F75

F71  HERBAL ANTIOXIDANT NETWORKS AND SKIN HOMEOSTASIS AT THE LIMIT — Tests botanical antioxidant-mixture interaction with a blinded 2×2 ingredient-by-dose factorial and measured free active concentrations. Matched single-active and vehicle controls distinguish chemical synergy from dissolution bias; precipitation and toxicity impose hard stops.

F72  NANOCARRIER TRANSPORT AND LOCAL ENERGY DISSIPATION IN SKINCARE AT THE LIMIT — Measures actuation energy per independently recovered microgram transported through a phantom. Equal-flux passive carriers, metered power and matched temperature challenge apparent active-delivery gains caused by externally supplied heat; excessive local heating vetoes release.

F73  SKIN MICROBIOME STABILITY AND ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE AT THE LIMIT — Measures time for a perturbed nonclinical skin community to return to a registered composition-distance threshold. Masked inoculum strata, contamination blanks and absolute counts test whether apparent microbiome resilience instead reflects introduced cells; pathogen growth is a stop condition.

F74  CELLULAR DAMAGE MEMORY AND REVERSIBILITY BOUNDARIES IN SKIN AT THE LIMIT — Tracks residual stress-associated epigenetic response by cell lineage after challenge withdrawal. Blinded single-cell survival and washout controls separate persistent stress memory from selective loss of damaged cells; reversibility is not inferred if an irreversible component is unidentifiable.

F75  SKIN EPIGENETIC AGE AND MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT — Challenges a frozen methylation-age proxy on held-out batches after cell-mixture correction. External calibration, subgroup uncertainty and matched conventional clocks distinguish molecular age evidence from altered cell composition; transfer-bias limits must be met before any age inference.

 

 

SECOND RESEARCH UNIT / CONTROLS, FORECASTS & SAFETY

Research Unit II · F76–F80

F76  BIOLOGICAL VERSUS APPARENT SKIN AGING AT THE LIMIT — Separates optically apparent skin age from an independently calibrated biological-age proxy. Masked lighting, makeup and camera perturbations test whether visual improvement occurs without molecular change; appearance scoring must not be interpreted as rejuvenation or diagnosis.

F77  CLOSED-LOOP INTELLIGENT SKINCARE AND SKIN-STATE FEEDBACK AT THE LIMIT — Tests bounded skincare feedback control by skin-phantom settling time. Equal-sampling open-loop and frozen PID baselines with hidden sensor noise distinguish real controller gain from higher monitoring frequency; unknown state or unsafe output requires abstention.

F78  AI PERSONALIZED SKINCARE AND LONGITUDINAL SKIN RESPONSE PREDICTION AT THE LIMIT — Evaluates 30-day individualized response forecasts on fully withheld people and future days. Seasonality shifts and identity-leakage tests challenge inflated AI accuracy against persistence and calendar-only baselines; weak subgroup calibration triggers a stop.

F79  SMART FACIAL MASK SENSING AND HYDRATION FEEDBACK CONTROL AT THE LIMIT — Measures smart-mask sensing-to-release lag against gravimetric hydration truth. Dummy humidity loads and equal-capacity passive masks expose capacitive drift mistaken for water transfer; excess release or irritation sentinels impose non-negotiable vetoes.

F80  ADAPTIVE HERBAL SKINCARE FORMULATION AND SAFETY OPTIMIZATION AT THE LIMIT — Estimates the share of pre-registered botanical formulation proposals meeting every locked chemistry and safety criterion. Unseen raw-material batches, coded ingredients and blinded toxicology compare adaptive optimization with conservative recipes; unsafe searches cannot count as success.

Physical Scope, Falsifiability & Evidence Status

The research designs emphasize traceable botanical lots, nonclinical cells, authorized ex-vivo references, skin-like phantoms, calibrated standards, blinded perturbations and independently measurable endpoints. Equalized sampling, material, energy and analysis budgets are required for fair baseline comparisons. Safety vetoes, identity integrity, uncertainty and unselected trial denominators are never traded away for mean performance.

The introductions identify mother-methodology DOI anchors 10.5281/zenodo.23480803, 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 as editorial lineage only. External DOI metadata, source-to-claim relevance, units and specialist scientific validity remain subject to independent verification. No human skin rejuvenation, therapeutic effectiveness or product-performance outcome is established.

Research Gate Evolution & QA Boundary

The source v1.2 release states that the 200 Research Gate pages per book (PDF pp. 538–737) were rebuilt from two candidate causal mutations for each Gate, while other pages were retained from v1.1. Source automation reported no exact repeated Gate questions or annotations and passed lexical screening; it does not establish 2,000 scientifically independent mechanisms. Physics, derivations, DOI relevance, experiments and full-page human visual review remain partial or pending.

metadata.title: Preventive effect of Dinoprostone (Prostaglandin E2) on testosterone-induced prostatic hyperplasia in a rat model
metadata.description:
Background: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a popular age-linked ailment featured by prostatic enlargement and urinary obstruction. Dinoprostone (DINO) is prostaglandin E2 having anti-proliferative and anti-inflammatory actions.

Objective: This research attempted to assess the effect of DINO vs. finasteride (FINA) on testosterone (TEST)-induced BPH in rats.

Methods: 40 adult male rats were haphazardly separated into 4 groups (n = 10); namely control, TEST, TEST + FINA, and TEST + DINO. BPH was induced with subcutaneous TEST (3 mg per kg per day) for 4 weeks. FINA (5 mg per kg) and DINO (7 mg per kg) were delivered orally.

Results: TEST administration led to marked prostatic enlargement and hyperplasia, paralleled by remarkable elevations in PCNA, DHT, 5α-reductase, β-catenin, ERβ, pro-inflammatory IL-6, and pro-fibrotic TGF-β and VEGF mediators. FINA and DINO effectively attenuated these alterations, restoring prostate weight and histoarchitecture, downregulating β-catenin and ERβ, ameliorating PCNA expression, and suppressing DHT and 5α-reductase activity. Both drugs modified inflammatory and angiogenic mechanisms and corrected PPAR-γ expression and regulated BCL-2 levels, indicating diminished apoptosis. While FINA surpassed DINO in inhibiting DHT, IL-6, and β-catenin expression, both treatments were equally effective in terms of anti-hypertrophic, anti-inflammatory, and anti-angiogenic actions.

Conclusions: DINO demonstrated promising anti-BPH effects comparable to FINA, acting via EP receptor-mediated modulation of prostatic growth and inflammation. These findings are viewed as preliminary and warrant further investigations of DINO for BPH treatment.

metadata.title: CCID-Epigenome: evidence-convergent prioritization of partial-reprogramming CpGs
metadata.description: A sequential, evidence-convergent workflow that prioritizes DNA methylation CpGs associated with maturation-phase transient reprogramming (MPTR) as candidate loci for direction-specific epigenome-editing experiments, and evaluates whether their methylation directions oppose independent cellular aging trajectories. Includes donor-robustness analysis, perturbation-network evidence, regulatory annotation, score-layer sensitivity analysis, and orthogonal validation against independent transient-reprogramming, replicative-aging and multidonor fibroblast-lifespan datasets.

**An ELAPOR1-linked immune–metabolic axis in CXCR5+ T follicular helper cells predicts poor prognosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma**

This repository contains the R scripts, the auxiliary mapping tables and the small result tables
that reproduce every computational figure and table in the manuscript from public data sources.
All large input matrices are **not** distributed here — they are public, and three of them exceed
the 100 MB GitHub file limit. `data/README.md` lists each one and where to download it.

metadata.description:
EXTREME RESEARCH MONOGRAPH

Longevity Biomarkers Microrobotic Sampling and Trustworthy Biosensing at the Limit

English Introduction and Publication Abstract

Research coupling

Longevity biomarkers × microrobotic sampling × trustworthy biosensing

Evidence firewall

Level 1 sample fidelity → Level 2 aging mechanism validity → Level 3 meaningful health outcome prediction

Book architecture

750 pages | 219,119 extracted English words | 82 chapters | 410 research sections | 30 linked derivations | 200 Research Gates

Scientific status

Prospective non clinical research architecture with explicit uncertainty abstention and stop boundaries

Publication Abstract

This research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for measuring dynamic longevity biomarkers without allowing the act of sampling, transport, storage, sensing, calibration, or computation to manufacture the apparent biology. Its central premise is simple but demanding: a biomarker has scientific value only when the sample remains traceable, the measurement remains calibrated, the proposed aging mechanism survives competing explanations, and the released result retains an uncertainty boundary appropriate to its intended use.

Microrobotic sampling is treated as a candidate laboratory capability rather than an assumed improvement. The reference domain is closed microfluidics, organ on chip systems, bench top modules, authorized ex vivo samples, and separately governed prospective research. A successful robot trajectory does not establish preserved biology. Greater analytical sensitivity does not establish mechanism specificity. A younger biological age score does not establish that an intervention improves healthspan or survival.

The Three Level Evidence Firewall

Level 1 Measurement Science. Demonstrate that collection, motion, contact, field exposure, storage, preprocessing, and sensing do not alter the target state beyond a preregistered budget. Preserve sample identity, mass balance, raw evidence, calibration ancestry, and covariance aware uncertainty.

Level 2 Aging Biology. Demonstrate that the biomarker reflects a specified aging mechanism rather than tissue composition, acute stress, disease, medication, circadian state, matrix interference, batch effects, or platform drift. Require orthogonal assays and mechanism specific perturbations.

Level 3 Longevity Intervention Research. Test whether biomarker change predicts or mediates meaningful function, healthspan, morbidity, or mortality. Association is not intervention benefit. Changing a score cannot be equated with changing health without independent prospective evidence.

Candidate Research Expression

Qvalid = Pintact × Ptrace × Pmechanism × Poutcome − Dsample − Uchain − Bintervention

The expression is a research ledger rather than a universal biological law. Each probability must be estimated within a declared sample matrix, platform, population, time horizon, and claim level. Sample damage, chain uncertainty, unauthorized use, and irreversible harm are veto conditions; they cannot be compensated by an attractive aggregate score.

Five Layer Research Architecture

Sample Truth and Claim Contract. Defines specimen identity, permitted use, exposure limits, claim level, strong comparator, vetoes, exclusions, and abstention.

Microrobotic Physics and Preanalytics. Measures flow, diffusion, wall effects, adhesion, shear, heat, field exposure, contact, dead volume, recovery, storage, and matrix change.

Aging Mechanism Validation. Separates mechanism specific biology from disease, cell mixture, tissue discordance, acute physiology, circular composite construction, and attractive but noncausal narratives.

Metrology and Longitudinal Inference. Binds raw signals, calibration functions, reference ancestry, detection limits, covariance, drift, personal baselines, irregular time series, and transportability.

Outcomes Governance and Successor Control. Requires meaningful outcomes, harms, consent, privacy, subgroup calibration, portability, negative result preservation, independent reconstruction, and the right to retire the system.

Minimum Verifiable Prototype

A blinded study divides matched biological reference material into three arms: candidate microrobotic sampling, a strong manual or passive microfluidic comparator, and a time matched unhandled control where feasible. The study records device motion, force, flow, temperature, contact time, surface history, sample recovery, raw detector output, preprocessing, calibration, uncertainty, and every rejected event. A hidden disturbance such as a coating lot change, dwell time extension, temperature excursion, or reference offset is introduced. The system must detect the invalidity, preserve the failure state, and abstain before the result is promoted.

Only after sample fidelity is demonstrated does the program test whether the selected biomarker responds to a mechanism specific perturbation. Only after mechanism validity is established does a separate prospective study ask whether the marker adds calibrated information about function, disease, healthspan, or survival beyond chronological age and established clinical measures.

Research Contributions

• A three level evidence firewall that prevents sampling feasibility from becoming an aging mechanism claim or clinical conclusion.
• Thirty mathematical and physical derivations connected to chapter corridors, experiments, failure tests, and Research Gates.
• Eighty two chapters covering sample truth, microfluidic physics, preanalytics, aging biology, biosensor metrology, longitudinal models, interventions, and governance.
• Two hundred detailed Research Gates designed as future research entry points with baselines, required evidence, competing explanations, stop conditions, and successor packets.
• A lifecycle design in which manual methods, passive fluidics, classical sensors, or the retirement of a popular biomarker can legitimately defeat the more complex system.

Central Scientific Boundary

This work does not claim that microrobots currently provide autonomous human body sampling, diagnosis, therapy, or life extension. It does not treat every age associated signal as a causal hallmark, and it does not recommend personal medical action. Clinical translation would require independent analytical validation, ethical review, regulatory authorization, clinical performance studies, harm monitoring, and post deployment surveillance.

Suggested English Description

Longevity Biomarkers, Microrobotic Sampling and Trustworthy Biosensing at the Limit is a 200,000 word class research monograph on the evidence required to measure biological aging without corrupting the sample or overstating the result. Across eighty two chapters, thirty linked derivations, and two hundred Research Gates, it integrates microscale transport, sample preservation, preanalytical control, aging biology, metrological traceability, longitudinal inference, intervention studies, and successor governance. The book enforces a strict three level firewall: preserved measurement must be demonstrated before mechanism validity, and mechanism validity before meaningful health outcome prediction. Its purpose is not to promise life extension, but to make future longevity research more testable, reconstructable, and capable of saying no.

metadata.title: Wounded Sovereignty: The Fisher King, Post-Drug Syndromes, and the Mythology of the Creative Core
metadata.description: A medieval story describes an injury that medicine is only beginning to address. In the Grail legends, the Fisher King is a sovereign wounded in the thigh or groin, the generative center and seat of the life force, sometimes by a sacred lance from his own castle. The wound will not heal: he neither dies nor recovers, and his kingdom becomes a waste land while he waits for a question no one thinks to ask. The legend reads almost like a prophecy of post-drug syndromes (PDS), illnesses that outlast the drug that caused them and one branch of the wider family of post-exposure syndromes (PES). Post-SSRI sexual dysfunction (PSSD), post-finasteride syndrome (PFS), and post-Accutane syndrome (PAS), which damage sexual function and emotional life, are paradigm cases. Routine tests are usually normal, even though molecular differences, including altered DNA methylation, have been found in affected patients. Pharmacovigilance, though, is currently built for acute reactions, rather than lasting harm. The legend’s central image, a suspended state that ordinary remedies cannot shift, aligns with the hypothesis that the drugs push the organism into a self-sustaining alternative stable state, or trapped set. The paper’s central argument is that these injuries strike the sovereignty the king embodies, in three forms (decisional, bodily, and testimonial), each creating a distinct obligation for medicine: to support informed decisions, to investigate and treat, and to listen accurately. Patients meet both testimonial and hermeneutical injustice: their testimony is discounted, and because medicine expects these adverse effects to end when the drug ends, their experience lacks a recognized pattern. The legend supplies one. Because these syndromes persist, they could accumulate into a population-scale crisis. PDS and PES are also numerous, and each is counted, if at all, on its own; but their collective and cumulative burden remains unknown. The waste land is a metaphor for that burden on society: left unaddressed, it poses a potential civilizational risk. The legend’s resolution points the way: the king cannot heal himself, and his healing is catalyzed only when a seeking knight finally asks the right question, “What ails you?”

metadata.title: Intron Retention: Organisation, Genome and Biological Roles and Associated Diseases
metadata.description: Alternative splicing expands transcript and protein diversity by generating multiple isoforms from individual genes. Intron retention (IR), a major form of alternative splicing, occurs when intronic sequences remain in mature RNA transcripts and is now recognized as a regulated mechanism of post-transcriptional gene control. IR can influence mRNA stability, localization, translation, and degradation, leading to transcript clearance through nonsense-mediated decay, nuclear retention, or production of alternative protein isoforms. Its regulation involves splice-site features, cis-regulatory elements, chromatin state, DNA methylation, transcriptional kinetics, and splicing factors. IR displays cell- and tissue-specific patterns and contributes to development and cellular responses to stresses such as hypoxia, heat, and infection. Aberrant IR is associated with cancer, neurodegeneration, aging, and immune dysfunction and may contribute to altered protein function and the generation of immunogenic peptides. Advances in RNA sequencing, long-read technologies, and computational tools have facilitated genome-wide detection and functional analysis of IR. This review summarizes current knowledge of the mechanisms, regulation, detection, function and biological significance of IR, with emphasis on its roles in normal cellular processes, stress adaptation, and disease.

metadata.title: The Speed of Aging
metadata.description:
Abstract:

 

Background: Medicine has long treated chronological age—the years since birth—as a convenient measure of health. It cannot, however, reveal much about how well a person’s cells function, what capacity they have retained, or which illnesses may emerge. Work on molecular biomarkers, particularly DNA methylation at CpG sites, produced early epigenetic clocks such as Horvath and Hannum. Later versions, including PhenoAge and GrimAge, linked their estimates more directly to health risks. These clocks made biological decline measurable, but they mostly record changes that have already occurred and generally provide only a single-time-point reading. The test itself requires a venous blood draw, costly laboratory work, and a wait of several weeks for results. That gap makes it harder for people to see how daily health choices affect their biology, which can make preventive habits difficult to sustain.

 

Objective: This paper sets out the conceptual and clinical basis for Epigenetic Velocity, a system designed to replace occasional biological-age measurements with a continuous, real-time estimate of how quickly age-related change is occurring. It combines molecular epigenetics with non-invasive digital sensing and behavioral economics so older adults can receive usable, same-day feedback on cellular wear and repair.

 

Methods: The study pairs multi-omic molecular markers with validated digital biomarkers collected frequently under the clinical V3 Framework: Verification, Analytical Validation, and Clinical Validation. Targeted next-generation sequencing of the ELOVL2 gene, together with fourth-generation causal clocks—DamAge, AdaptAge, and CausAge—provides stable molecular baselines. Wearables can estimate pulse-wave velocity from photoplethysmography (PPG), measure parasympathetic heart-rate variability with RMSSD, and track sleep architecture through actigraphy. Incoming physiological data feeds computational models that assign daily velocity scores and adjust small interventions when a person’s readings change.

 

Results: Because biofeedback arrives quickly, it may provide dopamine-linked reinforcement that helps offset present bias and bounded rationality. People may also stick with these habits more consistently when they see improved health as something they could lose, especially under health-endowment models. The program focuses on habits such as increasing slow-wave sleep, using short cold exposure to activate RBM3, applying controlled heat to produce HSP70, and walking after meals, which has been linked to TET-mediated gene demethylation. A municipal longevity trial in Kobe found that digital micro-nudges helped participants preserve functional independence while slowing chronic metabolic decline. Epigenetic Velocity links molecular biology to the health decisions people make every day. If Japan incorporated this non-invasive, people-focused method into a national program such as Society 5.0, healthcare could detect risks in real time and help prevent illness before treatment becomes necessary.

metadata.title: Integrative Analyses of DNA Methylation and Gene Expression of Immune Checkpoint Genes in Glioblastoma
metadata.description:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor with poor survival. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) show promise in many cancers, their efficacy in GBM is limited. Epigenetic regulation, such as DNA methylation, may influence immune checkpoint gene expression and contribute to therapy resistance. This study investigated the association between DNA methylation and expression of immune checkpoint genes in GBM, identified genes potentially contributing to resistance against ICIs, and evaluated the potential of combining ICIs with demethylating agents.

Data were collected from PubMed and TCGA, and 32 immune checkpoint genes were intersected across datasets. Pearson correlation analysis between methylation and expression was performed in R, followed by pathway enrichment analysis using Enrichr and protein–protein interaction network analysis using STRING.

Twelve genes showed the strongest negative correlations between DNA methylation and gene expression. These genes were enriched in immune-related pathways, including B cell receptor signaling, T cell receptor signaling, and negative regulation of lymphocyte proliferation, cytokine production and interferon production. The protein–protein interaction network highlighted LILRB1 and LILRB4 as potential immune checkpoint biomarkers in GBM. Overall, DNA methylation inversely affects immune checkpoint gene expression in glioblastoma, and a subset of strongly correlated genes represents potential targets for further research, including combination therapy with demethylating agents.

metadata.title: Chronic Inflammation as an Underlying Pathogenetic Mechanism of Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases: Molecular, Cellular, and Therapeutic Dimensions
metadata.description: Chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) constitute the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. Over recent decades, chronic inflammation has been increasingly recognized not merely as an epiphenomenon of distinct clinical entities, but rather as an overarching pathogenetic mechanism uniting neurodegenerative, metabolic, oncological, autoimmune, allergic, and age-related disorders. This underscores the imperative for a comprehensive analysis across its molecular, cellular, and therapeutic facets. Consequently, this review aims to map and synthesize contemporary data concerning molecular pathways, cellular effectors, and therapeutic modalities for the modulation of chronic inflammation through a literature-based approach. A narrative review of the scientific literature – encompassing experimental, clinical, and review studies – was conducted to elucidate the role of inflammation in the pathogenesis of chronic diseases. The findings establish chronic inflammation as a universal pathogenetic mechanism underlying various chronic non-communicable diseases. Its molecular architecture encompasses the NF-κB, JAK-STAT, MAPK, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, HIF-1α, and AMPK/SIRT1/PPARγ signaling pathways, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a complex cytokine network (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, IL-18, IL-33, TGF-β, and IL-10). Key cellular effectors span immune populations – including macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells, natural killer (NK) cells, T and B lymphocytes, and group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) – as well as non-immune and parenchymal cell lineages, such as adipocytes, hepatocytes, myocytes, fibroblasts, and senescent cells, all demonstrating marked phenotypic plasticity. Therapeutic modalities – spanning anti-cytokine agents, NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors, Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, metabolic modulators, antioxidants, natural phytochemicals, microbiome-directed therapies, senolytics, and targeted delivery platforms – exhibit substantial promise, yet demand a precision medicine framework owing to the context-dependent, pleiotropic nature of specific mediators and the inherent heterogeneity of inflammatory phenotypes. Chronic inflammation represents a pivotal pathogenetic driver underlying various chronic non-communicable diseases. Its molecular and cellular components form an integrated, highly dynamic network, offering a viable and high-value target for therapeutic intervention. High-priority research directions encompass multi-omics studies, the discovery and validation of robust inflammatory biomarkers, and the formulation of personalized and combinatorial therapeutic frameworks.

metadata.description:
🧬 BIOLOGICAL AGE & HUMAN MEASUREMENT AT THE LIMIT

Aging Clocks, Multimodal Biomarkers, Human State Measurement Science, and the Future of Healthspan Evaluation

What does biological age actually measure?

This flagship research volume explores one of the most important and unresolved questions in longevity science: how should we measure the biological state of a human being?

Chronological age tells us how much time has passed.

Biological age attempts to describe something more difficult — the changing condition, resilience, functional reserve, molecular state, organ performance, and recovery capacity of a living human system.

Yet no single clock or biomarker can automatically represent the whole person.

This book therefore moves beyond the idea of finding one universal “aging number” and develops a broader framework for Human State Measurement Science.

The research landscape includes:

DNA methylation and epigenetic clocks,
proteomic age,
metabolomic age,
glycomic biomarkers,
immune age,
organ-specific age,
brain age,
functional age,
recovery age,
resilience age,
wearable-derived age,
within-person clocks,
population-based clocks,
multimodal aging models,
clock disagreement,
clock reversibility,
biomarker uncertainty,
and longitudinal human-state measurement.

A central principle of the book is triangulation.

Molecular signals should be interpreted together with tissue-specific function, whole-person performance, recovery dynamics, longitudinal trajectories, and clinically meaningful outcomes.

A biomarker may change without health improving.

A clock may become younger without proving rejuvenation.

A model may predict chronological age accurately without measuring the biological processes that matter most for healthspan.

For this reason, the book repeatedly asks seven fundamental questions:

What is actually being measured?

Is the signal causally meaningful?

Does it correspond to improved human function?

Does it generalize across populations?

Is it stable and safe over long periods?

Can it translate from experimental models into real human biology?

And if it works, can it become a reliable and accessible measurement technology?

The deeper objective is not merely to estimate how “old” someone is.

It is to ask:

What state is the human system actually in?

This shift transforms biological-age research from age prediction into a broader science of human-state measurement — one capable of describing resilience, vulnerability, recovery, functional reserve, organ-specific change, and the trajectory of health across time.

The volume also treats disagreement between clocks not simply as measurement failure, but as potentially useful information.

Different clocks may observe different layers of the same organism.

The challenge is therefore not necessarily to force every measurement into one number, but to understand how multiple biological signals interact, diverge, recover, and predict outcomes that matter.

Designed as a large-scale Living Interactive research volume, the book contains 200 Research Gates.

Each Gate represents an unresolved research space rather than a final answer.

The Gates are designed to help future researchers move from uncertainty toward testable questions through structured attention to measurement, causality, longitudinal validation, functional meaning, uncertainty, translation, and scalability.

The purpose is not to eliminate the unknown.

It is to give the unknown a researchable form.

From age prediction,
to biological-state estimation;

from isolated biomarkers,
to multimodal measurement;

from static scores,
to longitudinal trajectories;

from correlation,
to causality;

from measurement,
to meaningful human function.

BIOLOGICAL AGE & HUMAN MEASUREMENT AT THE LIMIT is ultimately an attempt to build an early research architecture for a future discipline:

Human State Measurement Science.

metadata.title: Leptin Resistance, Obesity, and Gut Dysbiosis: The Role of Bitter Phytonutrients, Niacin, and Zinc [Review/Hypothesis]
metadata.description:
Leptin resistance is a hallmark of obesity and metabolic syndrome, yet its mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This paper proposes that leptin resistance is driven, in part, by a deficiency of bitter phytonutrients, niacin, and zinc—nutrients required for the gene transcription and function of bitter taste receptors. Bitter taste receptors, expressed not only on the tongue but also in the gut and hypothalamus, may support or co-regulate leptin receptors, as suggested by the efficacy of pomegranate ellagitannins in improving leptin resistance or which may be due to urolithin-A promotion of leptin receptors and/or promotion of PPAR and mitochondrial function. Bitter taste receptors and phytonutrients are also protective due to satiety hormone promotion including GLP-1.

This review synthesizes the literature on leptin, pomegranate polyphenols, bitter taste receptors, niacin, zinc, mitochondria, and the gut microbiome, and proposes a testable hypothesis: that restoring bitter phytonutrients, resistant starches, niacin, and zinc in the diet can improve leptin sensitivity, reduce inflammation, and support metabolic health.

The paper includes a hyperinflammation positive feedback loop (Figure 1) with a fully cited narrative (Appendix F), a clinical protocol (Appendix A), functional food guidance (Appendix B), a clinical guidance with a Table of histamine-producing microbial strains (Appendix C) and a diagnostic flowchart for histamine excess and Retinoid Toxicity (Appendix D), and a summary of genes associated with histamine sensitivity and Retinoid Toxicity (Appendix E).

This is a hypothesis-driven review with practical clinical translations—offering a framework for patients and practitioners to address leptin resistance through targeted nutrition and lifestyle changes.

Version 2 has an additional Figure and citations regarding GP109A receptor role in PPAR promotion and Nf-Kb inhibition.

Version 3 has two additional citations, (making 173 in total; a treasure chest).

Version 4 has a typo correction in gene identification numbers, and an expansion of section 2.1, with an additional citation to a companion paper:

metadata.description:
Analysis and figure-generation code, and derived (aggregate) result tables, for the study "A generator-matrix model quantifies the limited contribution of measured biomarkers to human mortality acceleration" (Tanigawa & Iwaki, 2026; manuscript submitted; an earlier version is posted on medRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.07.05.26356402).

The study asks, in one framework, how much of human mortality acceleration is captured by measurable molecular aging markers, whether the measurable part is causal, and whether it is reversible, using three orthogonal methods: (1) a Bayesian Markov generator-matrix model of hallmark-load dynamics with death as an absorbing state, fitted to NHANES (with linked mortality) and replicated in HRS; (2) two-platform cis-pQTL Mendelian randomization against parental-lifespan GWAS, calibrated with known-causal positive controls, with colocalization reported descriptively; and (3) a chronological-versus-causality-enriched damage clock battery on cellular-reprogramming datasets.

Contents: the analysis, figure-generation, verification and build scripts used for the reported results (Python; some R/shell), derived/aggregate result tables (CSV) with per-analysis findings notes, the posterior draws of the primary model, the Lean 4 structural-verification sources, pinned dependency files (environment/), DATA_PROVENANCE.md, LICENSE.md and CITATION.cff. Exploratory scripts from an earlier phase of the project that the manuscript does not use are not included. The manuscript text and rendered figures are NOT included (available via the journal article).

Data governance: this record does NOT redistribute restricted or licensed primary data (HRS individual-level data; UKB-PPP and deCODE pQTL summary statistics; GEO methylation matrices). HRS-derived tables are aggregate only (cell sizes >= 5), which the build script enforces. Obtain primary data from the providers as described in DATA_PROVENANCE.md.

Licensing: this record is released under CC BY 4.0; code in code/ is additionally licensed under the MIT License (see LICENSE.md).

Funding: JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP24K15812.

Version 1.2.0 adds the verification layer (an exhaustive audit of every numeral, table cell and figure label in the manuscript), three robustness analyses for the causation condition (colocalization sensitivity over cis-window and prior; Benjamini–Hochberg multiplicity; an outcome-GWAS sensitivity analysis against Timmers 2019), tests of IGF-1 and IGF2R, the posterior draws of the primary model, the build scripts, and the Lean 4 verification sources. Superseded outputs are retained with a PREV prefix so that each correction can be inspected. Headline values are unchanged: latent fraction 92.7% (NHANES), 91.5% (HRS), 89.1% (discretized re-specification).
